subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: C4.2 Transfers of energy and matter

questions.q: A population is:
options: All individuals of one species in an area at one time
The living and non-living parts of a habitat
questions.explain: A community is all populations; an ecosystem adds the abiotic environment.

questions.q: In an S-shaped growth curve, the population levels off at the:
questions.explain: Carrying capacity is set by limiting factors.

questions.q: A relationship in which one species benefits and the other is harmed is:
questions.explain: The parasite gains at the host's expense.

questions.q: An interaction in which both species benefit is:
questions.explain: For example, mycorrhizae and plant roots.

questions.q: The size of a mobile animal population is estimated using:
questions.explain: The proportion of marked recaptures estimates total size.

questions.q: Predator and prey populations often cycle because:
options: More prey supports more predators, which then reduce prey
questions.explain: This density-dependent feedback produces out-of-phase cycles.

questions.q: Organisms that make organic compounds using an external energy source are:
questions.explain: Producers form the base of food chains.

questions.q: About what percentage of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
questions.explain: Around 90% is lost as heat, in respiration and as undigested matter.

questions.q: Energy loss between trophic levels means food chains usually have:
options: A limited number of trophic levels
questions.explain: Insufficient energy reaches higher levels to support many organisms.

questions.q: Organisms that break down dead matter and recycle nutrients are:
questions.explain: Bacteria and fungi return nutrients to the ecosystem.

questions.q: A pyramid of energy is always upright because energy:
options: Decreases at each successive trophic level
questions.explain: Energy is lost at each transfer, so higher levels have less.

questions.q: Carbon returns from organisms to the atmosphere mainly by:
questions.explain: Respiration, combustion and decomposition release CO2; photosynthesis removes it.

questions.q: Burning fossil fuels affects the carbon cycle by:
options: Adding CO2 to the atmosphere faster than it is removed
questions.explain: It transfers long-stored carbon to the atmosphere, raising CO2.

questions.q: Competition between members of the same species is:
questions.explain: It is often intense because individuals need identical resources.

questions.q: Two different species competing for the same limiting resource show:
questions.explain: This can reduce the growth of one or both species.

questions.q: A food web models a community better than a food chain because it:
questions.explain: Most organisms have several food sources and consumers.

questions.q: Density-dependent limiting factors include:
questions.explain: These intensify as population density rises.

questions.q: A pyramid of numbers can appear inverted when:
options: One large producer supports many consumers
questions.explain: For example, one tree supporting many insects.

questions.q: During the exponential phase of growth:
options: Resources are plentiful and growth is rapid
questions.explain: Few limiting factors allow rapid increase.

questions.q: Decomposers are essential because they:
options: Recycle nutrients from dead matter back to producers
questions.explain: Nutrient recycling sustains producer growth.
